claims.text: A machine-learning predictive approach trained on high-entropy-alloy datasets can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The approach is applicable over a temperature range from -200°C to 1000°C.
Mass differences and force-constant differences act as phonon-scattering mechanisms in high-entropy alloys.
Patterns in high-entropy-alloy datasets correlate with low phonon thermal conductivity.
A machine-learning model can learn these patterns and use them to identify suitable low-phonon-thermal-conductivity materials.
The proposed approach will predict low-phonon-thermal-conductivity materials more accurately than current predictive approaches.
Improved prediction accuracy will result in enhanced thermal-insulation performance.
Molecular-dynamics simulations and empirical models are current predictive approaches for this task.
The proposed approach is limited to high-entropy-alloy compositions represented in its training datasets.
The approach may not generalize well to substantially different high-entropy-alloy compositions or to other material classes.
